constraints: Custom outputs are descriptive-only and must not include price, advice, or forecasts.
Custom outputs must be clearly labeled as custom in any API/client response.
Custom outputs must never overwrite canonical meta files.

drivers.what: Optional custom driver list; may be empty.

label.what: Custom regime label computed from canonical evidence + effective config.

custom_regime.what: Schema for custom threshold re-classification results (non-canonical).
custom_regime.why: Allows professional users to test alternative thresholds without mutating published canonical artifacts.

notes: Derived metrics are computed from numeric GOLD fields.
For each numeric gold field X, we publish X__ma7 and X__ma30 as rolling means.
min_periods=1 (early days are partial-window means).
Gate state is derived deterministically from META fields + this contract.
Historical META day-json are not backfilled with gate fields.

canonical.how: Stable hash over a canonicalized payload (chain, ruleset_id, label, asof_date, drivers) when NOT gated.
notes: If gated, determinism_hash may be null/absent; UI must treat regime label as UNKNOWN/DEGRADED.
Canonical hash must not be affected by any client-side custom threshold configuration.
canonical.what: Canonical identity hash for the regime snapshot computed by the pipeline.

custom.how: Stable hash over (canonical inputs + effective threshold config + custom outputs).
notes: Custom hash must never be presented as canonical.
Clients must explicitly mark custom outputs as custom (e.g., 'custom': true).
custom.what: Custom identity hash for a client-provided threshold config evaluation.

identity.what: Identity semantics to prevent canonical vs custom confusion.

confidence_score.how: Computed upstream in META; clamped to [0,1] in the engine.
confidence_score.what: A 0..1 data-quality confidence score used to gate regime labels.
confidence_score.why: Prevents overclaiming when coverage/quality/freshness are insufficient.

notes: A client may display these aliases explicitly so users can trace scorecard components to signals.
Some signals are transforms. Example: blocktime_instability is a transform of avg_block_time_sec; it should carry transform/current_raw metadata.
signal_aliases.what: Optional mapping from scorecard component keys to regime signal keys.
signal_aliases.why: Prevents confusion when scorecard uses compact component ids but signals use canonical metric ids.

current.what: Latest value for this metric/signal on as-of date.

current_raw.what: Optional raw input value when the signal is a transform.

pct_90d.how: Computed using <= counting within the last 90 finite observations (0..100).

transform.what: Optional transform metadata when the signal is not a raw metric.

z_robust.how: 0.6745*(x - median)/MAD; MAD computed over last 180 finite observations.

notes: signals is publishable evidence and must not change canonical identity hashes.
Missing data should be treated as unknown (null), never zero.
signals.what: Evidence surface for threshold re-parameterization: one entry per metric used by the regime engine.
signals.why: Enables customers to reproduce or customize classification without changing canonical labels.

notes: This dictionary is intentionally minimal in v1 and will be expanded.
Fields not listed here must be interpreted via their source schema (gold/meta/derived).
Regime labels are 100% descriptive (no price, no forecasts).
If gated, the headline label must be treated as UNKNOWN/DEGRADED in UI.
Canonical labels in META remain unchanged.
Custom labels must be explicitly marked as custom by any API/client.
Custom outputs should be traceable via identity_hash (see contract.identity.custom).
threshold_config_schema.what: Customer threshold configuration for custom classification.
